note: Pins for the toolchain this plugin puts ahead of the Windows PATH. `wild-stub` replaces the `wild` crate in every source: uutils reads its arguments through `uucore`, which uses `wild` to emulate Unix glob expansion, and that emulation corrupts arguments a POSIX shell has already resolved (see patches/wild-stub/src/lib.rs). `scripts/build-toolchain.mjs` publishes every name the components provide — the multi-call coreutils binary is hard-linked under all of its applets — because `find -exec`, `xargs` and `timeout` start a program and a builtin is not a file. Only `stdbuf` is withheld (this build produces no `libstdbuf` for it), and only the names `src/toolchain.ts` has no equivalent for are advertised: the rest are installed and never named. `packaged` records what was shipped inside the npm package: `scripts/pack-toolchain.mjs` copies the distinct binaries into `toolchain/win32-x64/` with a manifest naming every command each one provides, so an install needs neither Rust nor Go. `src/toolchain-artifact.ts` verifies those files against that manifest before anything runs. `uucoreErrno` marks the components whose messages have to name the OS error code when a file effect is refused: the plugin that runs them classifies a refusal by matching stderr, and the code is the only part of that message which does not depend on the host language. `coreutils` carries `uucore` in-repo and is patched by `patches/toolchain/coreutils/0002-keep-the-os-error-code.patch`; `findutils`, `grep` and `sed` resolve it from the registry, so `scripts/uucore-override.mjs` vendors the resolved version into the build cache, applies `patches/uucore/0001-keep-the-os-error-code.patch` to that copy and points `[patch.crates-io]` at it.

sources.name: coreutils
sources.why: Provides the programs a pipeline needs as real executables, which `xargs` and `find -exec` require because they cannot invoke shell builtins, plus `kill` and `timeout`. `stat`, `chmod` and `id` are opt-in features: enabling `stat` does not compile (uutils 0.12.0 then imports `uucore::fs::major`/`minor` and `uucore::fsext::statfs`, which that crate does not export for this feature combination), so it stays off and is recorded as a residual gap instead. `chmod` and `id` stay off deliberately (README records the residual-command decisions).

sources.name: findutils
sources.why: `find`, `xargs`, and `locate`. `testing-commandline` is a test helper the workspace also builds; it is not a command, so it stays out of the tools directory.

sources.name: grep
sources.why: `grep`. Young (78/128 GNU tests), so the corpus decides whether it is good enough or `ugrep` is preferred.

sources.name: sed
sources.why: `sed`. GNU sed is GPL, so this MIT implementation is the only distributable option.

sources.name: jaq
sources.why: `jq`, replacing the C implementation. Measured in section 28 of docs/research.md: 71/71 on the idioms a model writes, the corpus's jq cases and ten regex-dialect probes, then 40/48 on the extended list, where every remaining difference is a loud `unknown flag`/`undefined filter` on a rarely used feature (`$__loc__`, `--binary`, `--seq`, `have_decnum`/`have_literal_numbers`, `--run-tests`) except extreme-exponent formatting (`1E+1000` vs `1e1000`, the same value). Modules, `debug`, `stderr`, `input_filename`, `@uri`/`@sh`/`@html`/`@csv`/`@tsv`, `--slurpfile`, `--rawfile`, `input`/`inputs` and the whole regex surface agree. Built from source so the alias patch can reach it and so no prebuilt C binary stays in the chain.

local.name: posix-extra
local.why: The residual commands nothing permissively licensed provides on Windows: `which`, `cmp`, `diff`, `stat` and `ps`. Unlike the coreutils pipelines, `diff` uses the same diff engine oh-my-pi uses for its `diff` builtin.

goSources.name: goawk
goSources.why: `awk`, built from source instead of downloaded (A1 of sections 29 and 31 of docs/research.md). The released binary expands wildcards inside its own arguments on Windows (`expandWildcardsOnWindows`, ported from `mattn/getwild`), which `patches/toolchain/goawk/0001-no-windows-wildcard-expansion.patch` removes — a prebuilt cannot be patched, so the component moved to a source build. Being a source build is also what lets `patches/toolchain/goawk/0002-path-alias-in-argv.patch` apply the `/tmp` and `/<letter>` aliases inside the program itself (`dsh_path_alias.go`, the Go twin of the module the Rust components carry), which closes the last program-chain alias gap: `alias-chain-xargs-awk` was a `knownGap` until it landed (section 35 of docs/research.md). It is a POSIX-compatible awk (its own README, and measured against gawk 5.4.0), and the Go toolchain it needs is the lighter of the two prerequisites the awk cell faced: uutils/awk would have required LLVM/libclang from every builder. Section 32 evaluates the Rust alternative quinnjr/rawk and keeps this one: rawk agreed with gawk on 45 of the same 55 idioms, with `next`, `ORS`, `RS`, `exit` + `END`, a bare `length` and `split("")` wrong, while goawk agreed on all 55. Re-evaluate rawk once it fixes those and its own suite passes on this machine.
